description: Look up how a built-in model portfolio, canonical strategy or fund actually returned: seasonality by calendar month (average return, share of positive months, number of years and a t-statistic so a thin 'September effect' is not presented as a law), calendar-year returns with partial years labelled (optionally next to the S&P 500), trailing 1/3/5/10/20/30-year returns, and the best and worst year and month. Use it for 'is September bad for 60/40', 'what did All Weather return in 2022', 'how has SPY done over 10 years'. Pass exactly one of `template` (e.g. all-weather, classic-60-40), `strategy` (e.g. dual-momentum-gem) or `ticker` (a fund such as SPY, VTI, TLT, GLD, BND, VXUS); list_portfolios shows every valid id. For tickers outside that set, or custom allocations, use analyze_portfolio. Read-only and precomputed from the monthly refresh (proxy-extended monthly total returns), so it is instant and always says which month the data runs through. For risk and drawdowns use portfolio_risk; to compare portfolios use compare_portfolios.

benchmark.description: 'sp500' adds S&P 500 (SPY, proxy-extended) columns over the same months and the difference. Default sp500.

sections.description: Which tables to return: seasonality, calendar_years, trailing. Default: all three.

strategy.description: Canonical rule-based strategy id, e.g. 'dual-momentum-gem' or 'faber-trend-timing'. list_portfolios shows all 7.

template.description: Built-in model portfolio id, e.g. 'all-weather' or 'classic-60-40'. list_portfolios shows all 19.

ticker.description: A fund with precomputed proxy-extended history: any holding of a built-in portfolio or strategy or a fund with a history page, e.g. SPY, VTI, VXUS, TLT, GLD, BND.

years.description: Limit the calendar-year table to the most recent N years (e.g. 10). Default: all years.

name: portfolio_returns
